stories.headline: Ganjam on high alert amid 3rd cyclone alert
stories.title: Ganjam on high alert amid 3rd cyclone alert
stories.summary: The Collector instructed field-level officials to inspect all cyclone shelters and ensure the availability of drinking water, food, electricity, lighting and sanitation facilities.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Collector instructed field-level officials to inspect all cyclone shelters and ensure the availability of drinking water, food, electricity, lighting and sanitation facilities.

Brahmapur: With Ganjam district facing the possibility of a cyclone accompanied by heavy rainfall and strong winds on November 18 and 19, the district administration has sounded a high alert and initiated extensive precautionary measures, setting a zero-casualty target to safeguard lives, livestock and property.

A high-level preparedness meeting of departmental officials was held at Chhatrapur on Saturday under the chairmanship of Collector V Keerthi Vasan, who directed all departments to remain on alert and ensure coordinated action to meet any eventuality.
Drawing lessons from the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods, he stressed the need for advance preparedness rather than a last-minute response.
The Fisheries Department has been directed to ensure that all fishermen currently out at sea return to the shore by November 16.
Fishing activities will remain prohibited thereafter.
A public awareness campaign through loudspeakers will begin in all blocks from Sunday to sensitise people about the impending weather threat.
The BDOs will coordinate with elected representatives, Self-Help Groups and local communities to disseminate warnings and safety advisories.
Vulnerable people will be shifted to safer locations whenever necessary.
Pregnant women will be identified and moved to safer places in advance through coordinated efforts of the Health and Social Welfare departments.
Special arrangements have also been made for livestock protection.

Health centres will be stocked with essential medicines, including anti-snake venom injections, while the Animal Resources Development Department will make arrangements for the safe accommodation of cattle and other domestic animals.

stories.headline: Peak repo rate pegged lower at 6%, Dec hike on
stories.title: Peak repo rate pegged lower at 6%, Dec hike on
stories.summary: Mumbai: The rate-hike cycle is now expected to be shallower than previously anticipated, provided relatively softer crude oil prices and an easing of geopolitical tensions in West Asia persist into 2027, say economists.Most economists expect the terminal, or peak, repo rate at 6%, reversing earlier projections of 6.25%. While some still see the possibility of the policy rate rising to 6.25%, they consider it a low-probability outcome that would depend entirely on incoming data.Also Read: Food inflation to stay elevated; ICICI Bank sees 25 bps RBI rate hike in DecemberA rate hike in December, however, is widely expected, particularly after October retail inflation accelerated to 6.09%, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's 6% upper tolerance limit for the first time in two years.135864578The RBI is legally required to maintain the headline inflation between 2% and 6%.The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is scheduled to announce its rate decision on December 4. The committee raised the policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% at its last meeting in October, citing inflationary risks due to global uncertainties and deficient rains.Also Read: India's consumption story remains strong, but rural demand faces inflation risks: Report"Considering recent developments, we believe that the balance of probabilities has decisively shifted towards a 25-bps rate hike in December. We do not consider a further rate hike in February advisable, given the proximity to the union budget," State Bank of India chief economic adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh wrote in a report last week."The December 25-bps hike to be followed by a more data-dependent policy approach. This also leaves room for a downward revision in terminal-rate expectations," the report said.Indranil Pan, chief economist at Yes Bank said, "A hike in April remains a possibility, but the probability of the same may have weakened due to cooling global crude prices and steadying rupee."Brent prices fell sharply in early November as markets responded to expectations that the US would avoid another major military offensive after Democrats took control of both houses in the US.The recent correction in crude oil prices has tempered expectations of a relatively aggressive hiking cycle, with markets scaling back bets on multiple rate increases in the coming MPC meetings.Domestic inflationary risks also remain, due to the potential impact of El Nino, which could push up food prices. "Inflation has mostly peaked and while upcoming CPI prints may soften, they will continue to stay elevated, paving the way for measured hikes by the MPC. We expect the hiking cycle to be rather shallow," Barclays chief economist Aastha Gudwani said.

opening: Mumbai: The rate-hike cycle is now expected to be shallower than previously anticipated, provided relatively softer crude oil prices and an easing of geopolitical tensions in West Asia persist into 2027, say economists.
Most economists expect the terminal, or peak, repo rate at 6%, reversing earlier projections of 6.25%.
body: While some still see the possibility of the policy rate rising to 6.25%, they consider it a low-probability outcome that would depend entirely on incoming data..

We do not consider a further rate hike in February advisable, given the proximity to the union budget," State Bank of India chief economic adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh wrote in a report last week." The December 25-bps hike to be followed by a more data-dependent policy approach.
This also leaves room for a downward revision in terminal-rate expectations," the report said.

Indranil Pan, chief economist at Yes Bank said, "A hike in April remains a possibility, but the probability of the same may have weakened due to cooling global crude prices and steadying rupee." Brent prices fell sharply in early November as markets responded to expectations that the US would avoid another major military offensive after Democrats took control of both houses in the US.
The recent correction in crude oil prices has tempered expectations of a relatively aggressive hiking cycle, with markets scaling back bets on multiple rate increases in the coming MPC meetings.
Domestic inflationary risks also remain, due to the potential impact of El Nino, which could push up food prices.
"Inflation has mostly peaked and while upcoming CPI prints may soften, they will continue to stay elevated, paving the way for measured hikes by the MPC.
We expect the hiking cycle to be rather shallow," Barclays chief economist Aastha Gudwani said.
